subject: Biology
title: Reproductive Health
summary: Reproductive health (WHO) means total well-being in all aspects of reproduction — physical, emotional, behavioural and social. India was among the first countries to start national family planning (1951), later broadened into RCH (Reproductive and Child Health Care) programmes.

Contraceptive methods are natural, barrier, IUDs, oral pills, injectables/implants and surgical (sterilisation). An ideal contraceptive is user-friendly, easily available, effective, reversible and has few side effects.
Medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) is legal in India under specified conditions (MTP Amendment Act, 2017).
Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and infertility are major concerns; assisted reproductive technologies (ART) such as IVF, ZIFT, GIFT, ICSI, AI and IUI help infertile couples.

formulas.name: Natural methods
formulas.formula: periodic abstinence (days 10–17 of cycle);  withdrawal (coitus interruptus);  lactational amenorrhea (up to 6 months after parturition with full breastfeeding)

formulas.name: Barrier methods
formulas.formula: condoms (male — 'Nirodh'; female), diaphragms, cervical caps, vaults (reusable) + spermicidal creams/jellies
formulas.note: Condoms also protect against STIs and AIDS.

formulas.name: IUD types
formulas.formula: non-medicated (Lippes loop);  copper-releasing (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375);  hormone-releasing (Progestasert, LNG-20)

formulas.name: How IUDs work
formulas.formula: increase phagocytosis of sperm in the uterus;  Cu ions suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity;  hormone IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperm

formulas.name: Oral pills
formulas.formula: progestogens or progestogen–oestrogen combinations; taken daily for 21 days starting within the first 5 days of the cycle;  inhibit ovulation and implantation, alter cervical mucus;  Saheli (non-steroidal, once a week, CDRI Lucknow)

formulas.name: Emergency contraception
formulas.formula: progestogens or progestogen–oestrogen combinations, or IUDs, within 72 hours of coitus

formulas.name: Surgical methods
formulas.formula: vasectomy (part of vas deferens removed/tied);  tubectomy (part of fallopian tube removed/tied)
formulas.note: They are very effective but reversibility is poor.

formulas.name: MTP
formulas.formula: safe in the first trimester (up to 12 weeks);  MTP Amendment Act 2017: up to 12 weeks with one registered medical practitioner's opinion, 12–24 weeks with two

formulas.name: STIs
formulas.formula: gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis B, HIV/AIDS;  hepatitis B, genital herpes and HIV are not completely curable

formulas.name: ART methods
formulas.formula: IVF + ET (test-tube baby): ZIFT — zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) into fallopian tube;  IUT — embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into uterus;  GIFT — ovum from donor into fallopian tube;  ICSI — sperm injected into ovum;  AI/IUI — semen into vagina or uterus

formulas.name: Amniocentesis
formulas.formula: testing cells in amniotic fluid for genetic disorders; misused for foetal sex determination — legally banned in India

examples.title: Which ART?
examples.problem: A woman cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation. Which method?
examples.solution: GIFT — an ovum from a donor is transferred into her fallopian tube.

examples.title: Low sperm count
examples.problem: The husband has a very low sperm count. Which ART suits best?
examples.solution: Artificial insemination (AI) or intra-uterine insemination (IUI) with the husband's or donor's semen; ICSI if sperm can't fertilise on their own.

examples.title: ZIFT vs IUT
examples.problem: What is the difference between ZIFT and IUT?
examples.solution: ZIFT: zygote or embryo with up to 8 blastomeres goes into the fallopian tube. IUT: embryo with more than 8 blastomeres goes into the uterus.

examples.title: Why lactational amenorrhea works
examples.problem: Why is there no ovulation during intense breastfeeding?
examples.solution: Ovulation and menstrual cycles don't occur during intense lactation after parturition; this is effective only up to about six months after birth.

examples.title: Saheli
examples.solution: It is a non-steroidal oral contraceptive taken once a week, developed at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow.

examples.title: Preventing STIs
examples.problem: List simple ways to prevent STIs.
examples.solution: Avoid sex with unknown or multiple partners; always use condoms; seek a doctor early in case of doubt for early detection and complete cure.

topics.title: Reproductive health problems and strategies
topics.explain: Programmes create awareness about reproduction-related aspects, sex education in schools, birth control, care of pregnant mothers, post-natal care, importance of breastfeeding, equal opportunities for male and female children. Successful steps include lower maternal and infant mortality, smaller families, better detection and cure of STDs.

topics.title: Population explosion
topics.explain: World population was about 2 billion in 1900 and over 7.2 billion around 2011. India's population was about 350 million at independence and over 1.2 billion by 2011. Reasons: declining death rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR) and infant mortality rate (IMR), and more people in reproducible age. Statutory raising of marriageable age — 18 years for females and 21 for males.

topics.title: Contraceptives and side effects
topics.explain: Possible side effects include nausea, abdominal pain, breakthrough bleeding, irregular menstrual bleeding and even breast cancer — so they must be used under medical advice.

topics.title: Why MTP is needed
topics.explain: To avoid unwanted pregnancies due to casual intercourse or contraceptive failure, or when continuing the pregnancy could harm the mother or foetus. Misuse includes illegal female foeticide; unqualified quacks make illegal MTPs unsafe.

topics.title: Infertility
topics.explain: Inability to conceive despite unprotected sexual cohabitation; causes can be physical, congenital, diseases, drugs, immunological or psychological, and can be in either partner. Specialised health clinics help diagnose and correct some disorders. ART drawbacks: it needs very precise handling by specialised professionals and costly instruments and reagents, so only a few centres offer it and few can afford it; success is not guaranteed — the early embryo may not survive; emotional, religious and social factors also hold couples back. Legal adoption of orphaned and destitute children is one of the best alternatives.

topics.title: Complications of untreated STIs
topics.explain: Pelvic inflammatory diseases (PID), abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility and even cancer of the reproductive tract.

ratta: Copper IUDs: CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375;  hormonal: Progestasert, LNG-20.
Pills: 21 days, start in first 5 days;  Saheli weekly (CDRI).
MTP safe in first trimester (12 weeks).
ZIFT ≤ 8 blastomeres → tube;  IUT > 8 → uterus;  GIFT donor ovum → tube.
Hep B, herpes, HIV not fully curable.
ART limits: costly instruments + specialised experts, few centres, early embryo may not survive;  alternative = legal adoption of orphans.
